doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Miles and Lockjaw Davis playing How High the Moon in Philadelphia
summary: At a club date Miles got Lockjaw to sit in at a screaming tempo.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: I think it was the Blue Note or something like that in Philadelphia that was a prominent venue on the jazz circuit. When you toured playing jazz, you would inevitably play at that club. One of the most interesting experiences I ever had at this club was I came through Philadelphia touring with my own group – quintet, quartet or whatever the case might have been. Miles was appearing at this club, and it was exciting, as you would expect. Lockjaw was in the audience. I had never heard Lockjaw play. I knew about Lockjaw and I knew his reputation for being a wonderful jazz player, but I had never heard him live. Miles said, "J.J., I’m going to try to get Lockjaw to play a tune with us. Have you ever heard him play live?" I said, "No." He said, "Wait 'till you hear this, J.J." Sure enough, he got Lockjaw – Eddie "Lockjaw" Davis – to play How High the Moon about one hundred miles an hour, and it was a screaming, mind-blowing experience.
[laughs] What Lockjaw did was just – I'd never heard Lockjaw play that way, before or after.
It was just a brilliant situation that I have never forgotten.
